change: An actual returned credential receipt now owns its exact final auth control, transport boundary, publication and captured effects through a private consuming continuation.
behavior: The retained owner begins at the actual returned CredentialCommitReceipt. Its private receipt-instance identity binds the original frame and connection; copied field values cannot substitute another receipt or invocation.

The final UTF-8 control is sealed with byte length and SHA-256 under the existing collision-resistance assumption. Actual native writes or final BOSH-selected controls must match those bytes and the original owner before continuation. The digest is a check, not independent publication authority.

Native TCP and WebSocket action paths consume one transport start before their existing send/flush or live-write boundary. Successful exposure remains recorded even if later publication fails or is cancelled.

BOSH validates the exact final selected set before taking any holder, rejects duplicate identities, and consumes publication owners in FIFO order. An unbound success selected while a later bind success remains queued can consume only its own no-SQL publication; the queued bind owner remains untouched.

Restoration and supersession preserve the same unconsumed holder. A later failure or cancellation stops the selected continuation and retires abandoned exposed owners. Only successful publication/effect facts for every selected auth owner permit response bookkeeping and cache completion; a true callback or a terminal label alone is insufficient.

Publication uses captured route, Caps and notification inputs together with the existing current-owner checks. Transaction-entry, COMMIT acknowledgement and raw returned class remain separate; mismatches retain diagnostic facts and grant no further permission.

Inline SASL2 resume seals after the final control-envelope replacement. Handler return and publication retirement remain separate so a queued control can outlive its handler. Children are destroyed before retirement, including caught poll and destructor panics; Drop performs no SQL, retry or compensation.
compatibility: Existing protocol outcomes, native write/flush policy, BOSH queue/selection policy, publication SQL/query/rollback order, captured-effect order and deadlines are preserved.
Returned-only compatibility facades remain available. No new dependency, migration, session-wide latest-receipt authority, general executor or queue is introduced.
